description_full: Super Group (SGHC) Limited operates as an online sports betting and gaming operator. The company provides Betway, an online sports betting and casino offering; and Spin, a multi-brand online casino. It operates in Africa, the Middle East, the Asia-Pacific, Europe, North America, and South/Latin America. Super Group (SGHC) Limited is based in Saint Peter Port, Guernsey.

financial_summary: Super Group (SGHC) Limited is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $5.9B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 39% against a 10% cost of capital — a 30-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $294M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.50× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 32× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 69% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

Brand relevance decay — shifting consumer preferences and social-media-driven trends can strand inventory and invalidate positioning faster than product cycles can adapt.

sect: Its 11% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Cyclical median (7%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.45x).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-10.7% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 8% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 27% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 40% and a beta of 1.03, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.13 vs 5y 1.06), so read it loosely.
About $29.3M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 76% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $11.30 (margin of safety -3%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 47%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $8.98 to $14.60 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Consumer Cyclical peers: P/E 14.4 vs 18.8 and EV/EBITDA 8.5 vs 10.7 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 5.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 9 covering analysts target $17.67 on average, 52% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 10.1% annual cash-flow growth.
prof: ROIC of 39% clears the cost of capital of 9.7% by 30pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.87).
It converts 16% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 2.50x.
ROE of 21% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $388.0M.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.5% over 3 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 14%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 10.4% on average.
Analysts expect 2.7% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 68.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 25%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (13 sales, net $5.8M sold).
It returns 2.2% a year to shareholders (1.7% in dividends).
Short interest is elevated at 18.8% of the float, 10.4 days to cover.
people: With about 2,726 employees, each generates about $674K of revenue, 1.8x the Consumer Cyclical median, and revenue has grown 5.5% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $108K of free cash flow per employee.
